tagline.text: The "Big Dome" of Cubao, opened in 1960 and the site of Ali vs. Frazier

location.label: Location
location.text: Araneta City, General Roxas Avenue, Cubao, Quezon City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (depends on game and concert schedules)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day (3–4 hours for a game or concert, plus travel)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~5,000 (per ticket; varies widely by event and seat)

children.text: Araneta Coliseum is a large indoor arena that opened in Cubao, Quezon City, in 1960 and hosted the 1975 "Thrilla in Manila." Today it is one of Metro Manila's biggest venues for PBA basketball, university leagues, concerts and beauty pageants.

Araneta Coliseum is a domed indoor arena inside Araneta City in Cubao, Quezon City. Locals call it "The Big Dome," and since 2011 it has carried a telecom sponsor's name as the Smart Araneta Coliseum. Because the roof was built without supporting columns, the view is open from almost every seat. According to the official website, it was the largest indoor arena in Asia when it opened.
Its history begins with the opening card on
March 16, 1960

. The first event was a world junior lightweight title fight in which the Filipino boxing legend Flash Elorde beat Harold Gomes in the seventh round, and the official website says about 36,000 people packed the building that night. In 1975 Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier met here in the "Thrilla in Manila," which secured the arena a place in boxing history; it was temporarily called the Philippine Coliseum at the time. In 1981 a Mass celebrated by Pope John Paul II was also held here.

Today the arena is at the center of Philippine sport and live entertainment. The pro basketball league PBA played here from 1975 and became a regular tenant again after 1995. UAAP and NCAA university games, volleyball, boxing, the annual Binibining Pilipinas beauty pageant and world-tour concerts by international acts including K-pop artists all pass through. In 2023 it also hosted FIBA Basketball World Cup games, after upgrades that included a new LED video board.

For travelers, this is less a place to sightsee than a place to see something. One evening PBA game, or a university basketball season night among local fans, explains the Philippines' love of basketball at once. If a favorite artist is performing in Manila, this is also one of the most likely venues. This guide follows the order Korean travelers actually ask about: getting tickets, getting there, entry rules and getting home afterward.

blocks.title: A column-free dome that was among Asia's largest

children.text: Built between 1957 and 1959, the dome was described by the official website as the largest indoor arena in Asia and the largest clear-span dome when it opened. Look up from inside and there are no columns holding the roof, so the view is wide open. Dominador Lugtu was responsible for the design.

blocks.title: The stage of the Thrilla in Manila

children.text: The third fight between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier took place in this arena in 1975. It is still something of a shrine for boxing fans. We could not confirm whether there is a permanent exhibit inside, so check before you visit.

PBA games are the most popular spectator sport in the Philippines. The basketball configuration seats 14,429, and general admission is the cheapest and a good way to feel the local fans' energy. The schedule changes with the season, so check the official PBA calendar.

The UAAP and NCAA have been playing here since the arena opened in 1960. The school cheer squads and their performances are worth seeing, so you can enjoy the atmosphere even if you do not follow basketball. Rivalry games often sell out.

Manila shows by international artists are often held here or at the Mall of Asia Arena. In concert layout the capacity falls to about 9,679, lower than for basketball. Popular shows sell out right after sales open, so note the ticket release dates in advance.

blocks.title: Beauty pageants such as Binibining Pilipinas

children.text: The annual Binibining Pilipinas pageant is considered one of the arena's signature events. It is a chance to see Philippine pageant culture in person, but the date changes every year, so check the official announcements.

The arena sits right beside Gateway Mall, Ali Mall, Farmers Plaza and Novotel Manila Araneta City. If you have time after buying your ticket, you can eat in the malls, and after the show you can walk straight to the train stations.

items.title: PBA and university basketball plan
items.subtitle: A half-day schedule built around an evening game

children.text: Arrive at the Cubao train station and look around Araneta City. Have a light meal at Gateway Mall and withdraw cash from an ATM.
Check the entry lines and gate colors around the arena. Large bags are not allowed in, so leave them at your hotel.
When the doors open, pass the security check, enter and find your seat. Buy food and drinks sold inside.
Watch the game, including the opening show and the player introductions before tip-off.
After the game, rather than rushing out, wait a little for the crowd to thin, then head to the station or the taxi bay.
Game times and entry times differ by tournament and date. Follow the time printed on your ticket and the organizer's announcements first.
Arrive early and see whether there is a merchandise line or a fan gathering. Follow the official instructions for the lines.
According to official guidance, entry lines usually start forming from 2 p.m. Line up at the gate for your seating section.
When the doors open, pass the security check and enter. Note the emergency exits shown in the on-screen instructions.
Enjoy the show. With encores, it often runs around three hours.
After the show, the taxi bay and the train stations are both crowded, so walk a little farther before calling a Grab, or rest at a nearby restaurant first.
From NAIA, a taxi or Grab is the simplest way to reach Cubao. Depending on traffic it can take
over 1 hour
, so leave extra time on show days.
The Araneta City bus terminal serves provincial and airport-bound routes, so check locally which routes are currently running.
Cubao sits on EDSA, and traffic is heavy at rush hour (weekday evenings). Allow plenty of travel time.
The MRT-3 Araneta Center–Cubao station is on the EDSA side, and the LRT-2 Araneta Center–Cubao station is on the Aurora Boulevard side. Both connect to Araneta City by elevated walkways.
From the Makati side, take MRT-3 northbound. We could not confirm the last train times, so if you plan to travel after a show, check the operating hours in advance.
There is no train station in BGC, so either take a Grab or taxi, or ride to an MRT-3 station and go north.
There is a taxi bay and a Grab pick-up point on General Malvar Street near Gateway Mall. The lines are very long after big events.
The Main Avenue stop of the EDSA Busway is a few hundred meters south of Araneta City.
The south parking garage next to the arena has roughly 1,000 slots, and Araneta City as a whole is said to have about 7,000. On event days they fill up early.
When EDSA and Aurora Boulevard are jammed, the advice is to use side roads such as P. Tuazon Boulevard or Main Avenue.
What decides the best time to visit is what is on, not the season. The building is indoors, so events go ahead in the rainy season, but traffic around Cubao gets worse when it rains hard.
PBA and university league seasons change each year, so it is hard to give a fixed time of year. The most reliable approach is to check the official schedule and the ticket seller before you go.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Year-end shows tend to cluster, so tickets sell quickly.
The hall is air-conditioned, but prepare for the heat on the way and while queuing.
Umbrellas are prohibited items, so use one on the way and deal with it before you go in.

Novotel Manila Araneta City stands right beside the arena, and many concert-goers stay there. Cubao and the rest of Quezon City have plenty of other lodging. Rooms fill quickly on event days, so we suggest booking your hotel first as soon as your plans are set.

Most meals can be handled inside Araneta City. There are many restaurants and fast-food outlets around Gateway Mall, Ali Mall and Farmers Plaza, and more around Coliseum Circle near the arena. If you have time, a sit-down dinner by taxi in Tomas Morato or Katipunan is also a good choice. Food and drinks are sold inside the arena, and canned beer is poured into a disposable cup.
Buy tickets only through Ticketnet online, official outlets, or the places the organizer designates. Resale and scalper tickets have led to known cases of fake tickets.
Lost or damaged physical tickets are reportedly not replaced. Keep them safe, along with a photo on your phone.
Entry lines start forming around 2 p.m. Security checks take time, and the guidance is to come 60–90 minutes early.

Gates are divided by color. Green is for Patron and Lower Box A, Red is for Lower Box B and Upper Box, Yellow is for general admission, and the 2nd-level Southlink entrance is for all sections except general admission. Check your ticket section and go to the matching gate.
Bring only one small bag. Large bags can be left at the baggage counter in the Green Gate interior lobby or at the Yellow Gate, but the lines are long.
Once you leave, you cannot come back in. Take care of restrooms and food beforehand.
As soon as you are inside, watch the emergency evacuation instructions on the screens and note your nearest exit.
The taxi bay line is long after a show. If you plan to use the train, check the last train time in advance.
Rules on cameras and recording devices differ by event. Check the notice for your event on whether cameras are allowed.
On event days, traffic around Cubao is very heavy and the entrances are crowded, so keep valuables in front of you and set out early.

Glass bottles, cans, hard plastic containers, umbrellas, pointed objects, large banners, outside food and drinks, and smoking are restricted or not allowed. Rules differ by event, so check the latest announcements.
It is easy to lose belongings at crowded entrances and when leaving. Keep your phone and wallet in your front pocket.
Right after an event, the taxi bay and Grab requests are swamped. Using a licensed taxi at the bay or an app booking is the safer choice.

Children under 3 feet tall are reported to be allowed into PBA games and some concerts without a ticket, but a seat is not guaranteed. Family shows require a ticket for every age, so check the event rules.
In the surrounding area, stick to busy main streets and routes inside the malls rather than walking alone late at night.
A major park in the same city of Quezon City, reached by car. It is nice for a daytime walk.
A market-style shopping center in San Juan, good for shopping before or after a game. Travel time depends on traffic.
A large mall in the Ortigas area, south of Cubao.
A space on General Romulo Avenue with independent shops and restaurants, within walking distance of Araneta City.
